transcript: Part 2. Here are three things I think Broadway does better than the West End. And let's just start with the obvious one. Playbills. Everyone gets one for free. It gives you something to read at the theater and is also just a great memento to take home after the show. They do have programs in London, but you have to pay extra for them. They're usually between five and 10 pounds. And they also vary wildly from theater to theater. So, like, sometimes you'll get small ones like this, and other times you'll get massive bohemians like this. But not only does it cost a lot to collect these, but it's also very hard to store them because they're all so different. Another thing Broadway does that I love are the collectible sippy cups, similar to playbills. I love these as just a memento of the show. And yes, you do have to buy an overpriced to drink, but at least then you get a little keepsake. I also like that they come with lids. I don't know if London audiences are just cleaner than New York audiences are, but on the West End, people were getting, like, open top glasses of champagne, and if you gave that to a New York audience, it would just be everywhere. And finally, because Broadway theatres are a little bit newer than London theatres, I do find that they tend to have better sight lines. In London, I found that there were a lot of seats That were, like, behind a random structural pole, or on the extreme sides, and you had to, like, lean over the ledge. It also could have been the specific theatres I was at, but I personally found that Leg Room on Broadway is generally better than on the West End.
